summary: US equities enter June at fresh all-time highs (SPX 7,580 / NDX ~30,337) carried by AI momentum and Iran ceasefire hopes, while BTC trades near $73.5K under heavy ETF outflow pressure — its largest monthly exodus of 2026. Gold holds above $4,500 on geopolitical uncertainty, and WTI rebounds toward $90 as US-Iran deal progress stalls.
morning_report: Markets open June 1 with US stock futures flat after a banner May — the S&P 500 hit a 52-week high of 7,599 on May 29 and the Nasdaq gained ~8% in May, both riding an AI-powered rally and front-running hopes for a US-Iran ceasefire extension. Gold steadied above $4,500 after a volatile week: the pair remains technically capped below the 50-day SMA at $4,627, with MACD in negative territory, but geopolitical tension keeps a floor intact. WTI bounced toward $90 as weekend US-Iran negotiations failed to produce a finalized deal, with Trump reiterating demands over Iran's nuclear program and the Strait of Hormuz — oil remains binary and headline-driven this week. Bitcoin printed its weakest monthly ETF flow of 2026 at -$2.30B, breaking from two consecutive positive months, and technically sits below all key EMAs with RSI near 35; the $73,869 Fibonacci level is the immediate make-or-break level. Key macro catalysts this week: Jerome Powell remarks and May Manufacturing PMI today, JOLTS Tuesday, ADP/Services PMI/Beige Book Wednesday, Jobless Claims Thursday, and May NFP on Friday — all of which will shape Fed rate expectations ahead of the June 17 FOMC.
priorities:
1. Watch $73,869 BTC Fibonacci reclaim — a 3-day close above opens path to $77,877; failure risks slide to $68K zone.
2. NFP Friday (June 5) is the week's anchor macro event — labor data will recalibrate Fed rate expectations and reprice risk assets across the board.
3. Monitor US-Iran ceasefire headlines in real-time — WTI is the most headline-sensitive asset this week; a deal confirmation could drop oil $5–$8, boosting equities and pressuring gold.
4. SPX near all-time highs with RSI ~73 — overbought conditions warrant caution on new longs; watch for the first red weekly candle as a tactical signal to trim.
5. SCHW CEO insider buy of $1.85M on May 28 is a high-conviction signal vs. the stock's ~12% pullback — monitor for a mean-reversion entry opportunity in the financials space.

pairs.note: BTC trades near $73,500, below all major EMAs (20/50/100-day cluster at $76,400–$76,700), with RSI near 35 approaching oversold but not yet reversing. Spot ETFs recorded $2.30B in net outflows in May — the largest monthly exit of 2026 — with whales dropping 6,000+ BTC and long-term holders trimming 7.69% in one week. The $73,869 Fibonacci level must hold and close above on a 3-day basis to neutralize the bearish setup; a break below risks extension toward $68,000–$70,000.

Gold steadied above $4,500 on Monday as US-Iran ceasefire negotiations remained unresolved, providing a geopolitical floor. Technically, XAU/USD remains capped below the 50-day SMA at $4,627 and a descending channel resistance near $4,667, with MACD in negative territory and RSI ~42 — not yet oversold. The 200-day SMA at $4,405 is key downside support; conflicting ceasefire headlines make directional conviction low this session.

Nasdaq 100 closed May at ~30,337 after an 8% monthly gain, entering June with bullish momentum above the 30,000 psychological level supported by the AI demand trade. Both the S&P 500 and Nasdaq have RSI readings near 73 — near-term overbought — suggesting choppy, headline-driven price action in early June rather than a clean continuation. The AI trade (VST, TEM strong buys on sentinel) remains the structural driver; Middle East escalation risk is the primary downside catalyst.

SPX hit a 52-week high of 7,599 on May 29, closing at 7,580 — a ninth consecutive positive weekly close driven by AI stocks, tech earnings beats, and Iran ceasefire optimism. June stock futures are flat overnight, consistent with prediction market implied probability near a coin-flip for the June 1 session, suggesting mean-reversion caution after such an extended run. Key support is at 7,300; the bull case targets 7,700 with NFP and FOMC (June 17) as the next major re-pricing events.

WTI rebounded toward $89–$90 on Monday after falling to ~$87.20 last Friday when preliminary US-Iran ceasefire reports briefly surfaced; the deal remains unsigned and Trump reaffirmed demands, adding uncertainty. Oil posted a ~16% monthly decline in May on ceasefire hopes, but analysts warn any Strait of Hormuz supply recovery will be slow due to mines, infrastructure damage, and tanker delays — limiting downside. The pair is binary and headline-driven; a confirmed deal could push WTI toward $80, while a deal collapse could spike it back above $95.

Gold holds above $4,500 on unresolved US-Iran tensions but remains technically capped below the 50-day SMA at $4,627 with negative MACD; directional resolution tied to ceasefire and NFP outcomes.

SPX holds at record highs with expanding breadth and AI-driven momentum, though near-term overbought RSI of ~73 and June seasonality headwinds suggest choppy upside rather than a straight run to 7,700.
